facts.raw_span: A 56-year-old nulliparous woman presented 14 months after a supracervical laparoscopic hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
menorrhagia, pelvic pain, and large uterine leiomyomas
normal Pap smear
no chest radiograph or endometrial biopsy was obtained
an 18–20-week–size uterus (1518 g) was removed via prolonged mechanical morcellation without a containment bag
superficial pelvic endometriosis was noted and cauterized
weakly proliferative endometrium without atypia, adenomyosis, and leiomyoma
left lower quadrant pain, persistent cough, and shortness of breath
firm left lower quadrant abdominal mass and a fleshy lesion at the vaginal apex
multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest
poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis
grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma
A 56-year-old nulliparous woman presented 14 months after a supracervical laparoscopic hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
menorrhagia, pelvic pain, and large uterine leiomyomas
normal Pap smear
no chest radiograph or endometrial biopsy was obtained
an 18–20-week–size uterus (1518 g) was removed via prolonged mechanical morcellation without a containment bag
superficial pelvic endometriosis was noted and cauterized
weakly proliferative endometrium without atypia, adenomyosis, and leiomyoma
left lower quadrant pain, persistent cough, and shortness of breath
firm left lower quadrant abdominal mass and a fleshy lesion at the vaginal apex
multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest
poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis
grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma

concepts.why: The patient's history of supracervical laparoscopic hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with prolonged mechanical morcellation without a containment bag, combined with the presence of multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest, suggests the possibility of disseminated peritoneal leiomyomatosis.

The vaginal biopsy showing grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma, along with the presence of a firm left lower quadrant abdominal mass and multiple hypermetabolic masses, supports the diagnosis of endometrioid adenocarcinoma.

The patient's history of uterine leiomyomas and the presence of poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis, along with multiple hypermetabolic masses, raises the possibility of utine leiomyosarcoma.

The presence of multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest, along with the histological findings of poorly differentiated epithelioid cells, suggests the possibility of peritoneal carcinoma.
The patient's history of adenomyosis and the presence of a firm left lower quadrant abdominal mass, along with multiple hypermetabolic masses, raises the possibility of endometrial stromal sarcoma.

rationales.F05: Prolonged mechanical morcellation without a containment bag may have disseminated leiomyomatosis cells.
rationales.F06: Superficial pelvic endometriosis is a risk factor for disseminated peritoneal leiomyomatosis.
rationales.F10: Multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest are consistent with disseminated peritoneal leiomyomatosis or peritoneal carcinoma.
rationales.F11: Poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis are more typical of malignant tumors such as endometrioid adenocarcinoma or peritoneal carcinoma.
rationales.F12: Grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma is a definitive diagnosis that rules out other conditions.
